machine.note: The plan states this machine is an ASUS NUC14LNK, taken from Win32_ComputerSystem.Model. Measured on the probe run: the hostname is 'NUC14PROAI', Win32_ComputerSystem reports 'ASUSTeK COMPUTER INC. NUC14LNK LN', and the PCI subsystem id(s) are ['SUBSYS_88F21043']. The hostname and the subsystem id are consistent with a NUC14 Pro AI rather than an NUC14LNK. Both records are kept and neither is treated as the winner here; the M0 report reconciles them. Nothing in this map depends on which is right - the LUID table, the engine inventory and the counter path are all measured per LUID.

counter_source.note: The runtime does not use this path. It reads config/telemetry_map.json and matches instance names by LUID; see app/telemetry/pdh.py for why the ctypes value read is not usable on this machine.

direct_luid_link.reason: Measured on this machine: no CIM or Win32 source exposes a LUID together with a PCI device id. Win32_PerfFormattedData_GPUPerformanceCounters_GPUAdapterMemory carries only Name and memory counters; Win32_VideoController carries PNPDeviceID but no LUID; EnumDisplayDevicesW returns PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_64A0&SUBSYS_88F21043&REV_04 for all three display adapter entries and no LUID; Win32_LUID exposes no instances and MSFT_ComputeAccelerator is not a registered CIM class on this build. The mapping is therefore resolved from the engine taxonomy, with the evidence recorded per LUID.
